New: AI Market Pulse, our monthly round-up of the AI numbers that moved, checked and dated.

November's headline: the AI build-out started borrowing in earnest.

• Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta reported about $207B of capex for July–September, as each reports it.
• Free cash flow went negative at Meta (−$2.1B), Alphabet (≈−$9.1B) and Amazon (−$42.4B over 12 months).
• Between 26 Oct and 5 Nov, Meta, Oracle and Alphabet raised more than $70B of new equity and debt, at coupons up to 8.65%.

Also inside: the largest funding rounds (DeepSeek, OpenAI at $1.25T), token prices, assistant user numbers, and AI-attributed job cuts. Every figure dated and confidence-rated; the data is downloadable.

How big is the AI agents market? $49B, $155B, $468B or $985B by 2030, depending who you ask.

We put 30 forecasts side by side. Most of the gap is definitions: only the $49B median measures agent revenue.
li:
How big is the AI agents market, really?

The 2030 figure is quoted as $49B, $155B, $468B and $985B. We collected 30 published forecasts from 24 firms and found the disagreement is mostly about what's being counted:

• Standalone agent revenue (research firms): about $7–8B in 2025, a 2030 median of about $49B, most forecasts between $36B and $54B.
• Gartner's $985B (and $206.5B for 2026) counts all software with agentic features built in. Its standalone agents line is about $29B for 2026.
• IDC's $1.3T for 2029 is total AI spending.
• Bank of America's $155B and Goldman's implied $468B+ are value-capture estimates, not revenue.

Meanwhile 17% of organisations have deployed agents (Gartner) and Gartner expects 40%+ of agentic projects to be cancelled by 2027.

But October had just 1,265, the lowest month of the year, and AI is no longer the top stated reason. One month isn't a trend.
li:
US job cuts attributed to AI reached 121,401 from January to October 2026, more than twice the 54,836 for all of 2025 (Challenger, Gray & Christmas).

But the monthly picture turned: October had just 1,265 AI-attributed cuts, the lowest month of the year, and "market/economic conditions" has overtaken AI as the leading stated reason in 2026.

One month is not a trend. November's report will show whether this is a pause or a turn. And "attributed to AI" is the employer's stated reason, which can overstate or understate AI's actual role.
